name: Non-text Content
howToTest: Check every image, icon, chart and image button: informative ones need alt text that conveys the same information or function, and decorative ones need alt="" or to be hidden from assistive technology. Use a screen reader or an alt-text inspector to read each text alternative in context.

name: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
howToTest: For each prerecorded audio-only file, confirm a text transcript is provided. For each video with no audio track, confirm there is a text description or an audio track that conveys the same information.

name: Captions (Prerecorded)
howToTest: Play each prerecorded video that has audio with the sound off and captions on. Confirm captions are present for the whole video, accurate, in sync, and include speaker names and meaningful sounds.

name: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
howToTest: For each prerecorded video, watch it with your eyes closed and note any visual information you missed. Confirm that information is available through audio description or a full text alternative of the video.

name: Captions (Live)
howToTest: For live video streams with audio, confirm real-time captions are available and can be turned on. Watch a portion with sound off to check they keep up and are understandable.

name: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
howToTest: For each prerecorded video, confirm an audio-described version or description track is available. Listen without watching and check that important visual content, such as on-screen text and actions, is described.

name: Sign Language (Prerecorded)
howToTest: For each prerecorded video with audio, confirm a sign language interpretation is provided, either in the video or as a selectable alternate version.

name: Extended Audio Description (Prerecorded)
howToTest: Where pauses in the audio are too short to describe important visuals, confirm an extended audio description version pauses the video to fit the descriptions.

name: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
howToTest: For each prerecorded video, confirm a full text alternative is provided that includes all dialogue and describes all important visual information, like a screenplay.

name: Audio-only (Live)
howToTest: For live audio-only content, such as a radio stream or audio webcast, confirm a real-time text alternative such as live captioning is provided.

name: Info and Relationships
howToTest: Compare the visual structure with the markup: headings use h1 to h6, lists use list elements, data tables use th and caption, and form fields are programmatically grouped and labeled. Turn off CSS or use a screen reader to confirm the structure and relationships still come through.

name: Meaningful Sequence
howToTest: Read the page in DOM order with a screen reader or with CSS disabled. Confirm the content still reads in an order that makes sense, especially for multi-column layouts, cards and content positioned with CSS.

name: Sensory Characteristics
howToTest: Search instructions for references that rely only on shape, color, size, position or sound, such as "click the round button" or "see the box on the right". Confirm each also names the control or content in text.

name: Orientation
howToTest: Rotate a phone or tablet, or switch device emulation between portrait and landscape. Confirm the content works and is not locked to one orientation unless that is essential.

name: Identify Input Purpose
howToTest: For form fields that collect information about the user, such as name, email, phone and address, confirm each has the correct autocomplete attribute value. Check that browser autofill offers the right suggestions.

name: Identify Purpose
howToTest: Confirm the purpose of icons, regions and UI components can be determined programmatically, for example through landmarks, accessible names and standard semantics, so tools can adapt or replace them.

name: Use of Color
howToTest: Look for information conveyed by color alone, such as links in text, required fields, error states, chart series and status indicators. View the page in grayscale and confirm each still has a text, icon, pattern or underline cue.

name: Audio Control
howToTest: Load the page and listen for audio that starts automatically. If it plays for more than 3 seconds, confirm there is an easy-to-find control near the top of the page to pause, stop or mute it.

name: Contrast (Minimum)
howToTest: Measure text against its background with the DevTools color picker or a contrast checker. Normal text needs at least 4.5:1 and large text at least 3:1, including text over images, gradients and in hover or focus states.

name: Resize Text
howToTest: Zoom the browser to 200 percent and confirm all text grows and nothing is cut off, overlapping or hidden. On mobile, confirm pinch zoom is not disabled.

name: Images of Text
howToTest: Look for text rendered as an image, such as banners, buttons and quotes. Confirm real styled text is used instead, unless it is a logo or the visual presentation is essential.

name: Contrast (Enhanced)
howToTest: Measure text against its background with a contrast checker. Normal text needs at least 7:1 and large text at least 4.5:1.

name: Low or No Background Audio
howToTest: For prerecorded audio that is mostly speech, listen for background sound. Confirm there is none, it can be turned off, or it is at least 20 dB quieter than the speech.

name: Visual Presentation
howToTest: For blocks of text, confirm users can choose text and background colors, lines are no wider than 80 characters, text is not justified, line spacing is at least 1.5, and text resizes to 200 percent without horizontal scrolling.

name: Images of Text (No Exception)
howToTest: Look for any text rendered as an image. Confirm it is only used for pure decoration or where the particular presentation is essential, such as a logo.

name: Reflow
howToTest: Set the browser window to 1280 px wide and zoom to 400 percent, or use a 320 px wide viewport. Confirm content reflows into one column with no horizontal scrolling and no lost content or functionality, except for content like maps and data tables that need two dimensions.

name: Non-text Contrast
howToTest: Measure the contrast of input borders, focus indicators, icons, toggle states and meaningful chart elements against adjacent colors. Each needs at least 3:1.

name: Text Spacing
howToTest: Apply a text spacing bookmarklet that sets line height to 1.5, paragraph spacing to 2 times, letter spacing to 0.12 and word spacing to 0.16 times the font size. Confirm no text is clipped, overlapped or hidden.

name: Content on Hover or Focus
howToTest: Trigger every tooltip, popover and hover menu with the mouse and with keyboard focus. Confirm it can be dismissed with Escape without moving focus, the pointer can move onto it without it closing, and it stays visible until dismissed or no longer relevant.

name: Keyboard
howToTest: Put the mouse aside and use Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Escape and arrow keys to operate every link, button, form control, menu, dialog and custom widget. Confirm everything that works with a mouse also works with the keyboard.

name: No Keyboard Trap
howToTest: Tab through the whole page, including embedded widgets, video players, iframes and dialogs. Confirm focus can always move away again with standard keys, or that instructions for leaving are given.

name: Keyboard (No Exception)
howToTest: Operate all functionality with the keyboard only, with no exceptions, including drawing, drag-and-drop and map interactions.

name: Character Key Shortcuts
howToTest: Find any keyboard shortcuts that use a single letter, number or symbol key. Confirm they can be turned off or remapped, or only work while the relevant component has focus.

name: Timing Adjustable
howToTest: Look for session timeouts, auto-advancing content and timed tasks. Confirm users are warned before time runs out and can turn off, adjust or extend the limit at least ten times, unless the time limit is essential or over 20 hours.

name: Pause, Stop, Hide
howToTest: Find content that moves, blinks, scrolls or auto-updates, such as carousels, animations, tickers and live feeds. If it starts automatically and lasts more than 5 seconds, confirm there is a control to pause, stop or hide it.

name: No Timing
howToTest: Confirm no part of the content or task has a time limit, except for real-time events and non-interactive synchronized media.

name: Interruptions
howToTest: Look for automatic updates, alerts, popups and page refreshes. Confirm users can postpone or turn them off, except for emergencies.

name: Re-authenticating
howToTest: Let a session expire while partway through a form or task, then sign in again. Confirm you can continue without losing the data you entered.

name: Timeouts
howToTest: If inactivity can cause data loss, confirm users are told how long they can be inactive before it happens, unless data is kept for more than 20 hours.

name: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
howToTest: Review videos, animations and effects for flashing. Confirm nothing flashes more than three times in any one second, or that flashes stay below the general and red flash thresholds, for example by checking with PEAT.

name: Three Flashes
howToTest: Review all content for flashing. Confirm nothing flashes more than three times in any one second, regardless of size or brightness.

name: Animation from Interactions
howToTest: Turn on the operating system's reduce motion setting and interact with the page. Confirm motion animations triggered by interaction, such as parallax and zooming transitions, are disabled or can be turned off.

name: Bypass Blocks
howToTest: Load the page and press Tab. Confirm a skip link or landmarks and headings let keyboard and screen reader users jump past repeated navigation to the main content, and that the skip link moves focus there.

name: Page Titled
howToTest: Read the browser tab title on each page and view. Confirm it is present, unique, and describes the page topic or purpose, and that it updates on single-page-app route changes.

name: Focus Order
howToTest: Tab through the page and watch where focus goes. Confirm it follows a logical order that preserves meaning, and that opening dialogs or menus moves focus into them and returns it afterward.

name: Link Purpose (In Context)
howToTest: Read each link with its surrounding sentence, paragraph, list item or table cell. Confirm its purpose is clear, and flag links like "click here" or "read more" whose destination cannot be determined from context.

name: Multiple Ways
howToTest: Confirm there are at least two ways to find each page in the site, such as navigation menus, search, a site map or related links, except for pages that are a step in a process.

name: Headings and Labels
howToTest: Read all headings and form labels out of context, for example from a screen reader's headings list. Confirm each describes the topic or purpose of its section or field.

name: Focus Visible
howToTest: Tab through every interactive element on the page. Confirm a visible focus indicator appears on each one and is never removed with outline: none without a replacement.

name: Location
howToTest: Confirm users can tell where they are within the site, for example through breadcrumbs, a highlighted current navigation item, or a site map.

name: Link Purpose (Link Only)
howToTest: Read the list of links on the page out of context, for example with a screen reader's links list. Confirm each link's text alone identifies its purpose, and that links with the same text go to the same place.

name: Section Headings
howToTest: Confirm long content is organized into sections and each section starts with a heading.

name: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
howToTest: Tab through the page with sticky headers, footers, cookie banners and chat widgets visible. Confirm the focused element is never entirely hidden behind author-created content.

name: Focus Not Obscured (Enhanced)
howToTest: Tab through the page with all sticky and overlay content visible. Confirm no part of the focused element is hidden by author-created content.

name: Focus Appearance
howToTest: Tab to each control and inspect the focus indicator. Confirm it is at least as large as a 2 CSS px perimeter around the control and has at least 3:1 contrast between its focused and unfocused states.

name: Pointer Gestures
howToTest: Find features operated by multipoint or path-based gestures, such as pinch, two-finger swipe or drawing a path. Confirm each can also be done with a single tap or click, for example with buttons.

name: Pointer Cancellation
howToTest: Press the mouse or finger down on each control, move off it, then release. Confirm the action does not fire on the down event, or that it can be aborted or undone.

name: Label in Name
howToTest: For each control with a visible text label, inspect its accessible name in the DevTools Accessibility pane. Confirm the name contains the visible text, ideally at the start, so voice-control users can say what they see.

name: Motion Actuation
howToTest: Find features triggered by shaking or tilting the device. Confirm the same action is available through a normal UI control and that motion triggering can be turned off.

name: Target Size (Enhanced)
howToTest: Measure the hit area of each pointer target in DevTools. Confirm it is at least 44 by 44 CSS px, except for inline links, browser-default controls and targets with an equivalent elsewhere.

name: Concurrent Input Mechanisms
howToTest: On a touch device, connect a keyboard or mouse and use it alongside touch. Confirm the page does not block or ignore any available input method.

name: Dragging Movements
howToTest: Find features that use dragging, such as sortable lists, sliders, maps and file drop zones. Confirm each can also be done with single clicks or taps without dragging.

name: Target Size (Minimum)
howToTest: Measure each pointer target in DevTools. Confirm it is at least 24 by 24 CSS px, or that a 24 px circle centered on it does not overlap neighboring targets, unless it is inline in text, a browser-default control, has a larger equivalent, or its size is essential.

name: Language of Page
howToTest: Inspect the html element and confirm its lang attribute is present, valid, and matches the main language of the page content.

name: Language of Parts
howToTest: Find passages, quotes and links in a language other than the page language. Confirm each has a lang attribute with the correct language code, then listen with a screen reader to check the pronunciation switches.

name: Unusual Words
howToTest: Look for idioms, jargon and words used in an unusual way. Confirm a definition is available, for example inline, in a glossary, or through a linked definition.

name: Abbreviations
howToTest: Look for abbreviations and acronyms. Confirm the expanded form or meaning is available, such as on first use or through an abbr element or glossary.

name: Reading Level
howToTest: Run the main content through a readability checker. If it requires more than a lower secondary education reading level, confirm a simpler summary or supplemental content is provided.

name: Pronunciation
howToTest: Find words whose meaning is ambiguous without knowing the pronunciation. Confirm a pronunciation is provided, for example inline, in a glossary, or with ruby annotations.

name: On Focus
howToTest: Tab to each control without activating it. Confirm that receiving focus alone does not submit forms, open new windows, move focus elsewhere, or otherwise change the context.

name: On Input
howToTest: Change the value of each select, checkbox, radio and text field. Confirm that doing so does not automatically navigate, submit or move focus unless the user was told beforehand.

name: Consistent Navigation
howToTest: Compare navigation menus, headers and footers across several pages. Confirm repeated navigation appears in the same relative order each time.

name: Consistent Identification
howToTest: Compare components with the same function across pages, such as search, print or download icons. Confirm they use consistent labels, names and text alternatives.

name: Change on Request
howToTest: Look for automatic redirects, refreshes, new windows and focus changes. Confirm changes of context only happen when the user requests them, or that a mechanism to turn them off is provided.

name: Consistent Help
howToTest: If help mechanisms such as contact details, a chat widget, a help link or a FAQ link appear on multiple pages, confirm they appear in the same relative order on each page.

name: Error Identification
howToTest: Submit each form with missing and invalid input. Confirm each error is described in text, identifies the field in error, and is announced to screen reader users.

name: Labels or Instructions
howToTest: Check each form field and group for a visible label, plus instructions for required fields and expected formats such as dates or passwords. Placeholder text alone does not count.

name: Error Suggestion
howToTest: Trigger validation errors on each form field. Confirm the error message suggests how to fix the input, such as the expected format or valid range, when a correction is known.

name: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
howToTest: For forms that make legal commitments, financial transactions, or change or delete user data, confirm submissions are reversible, are checked for errors, or offer a review and confirm step before final submission.

name: Help
howToTest: Confirm context-sensitive help is available for form fields and tasks, such as instructions, examples or links to help content near the input.

name: Error Prevention (All)
howToTest: For every form that submits information, confirm the submission is reversible, is checked for errors, or offers a chance to review and confirm before final submission.

name: Redundant Entry
howToTest: Walk through multi-step processes such as checkout. Confirm information already entered is auto-filled or offered for selection rather than having to be typed again, unless re-entry is essential or for security.

name: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
howToTest: Go through sign-in and verification steps. Confirm none require a cognitive function test, such as remembering a password or solving a puzzle, unless pasting, password managers, an alternative method, or object or personal content recognition is supported.

name: Accessible Authentication (Enhanced)
howToTest: Go through sign-in and verification steps. Confirm none require a cognitive function test, including recognizing objects or personal content, unless an alternative method or assistance mechanism is offered.

name: Name, Role, Value
howToTest: Inspect each interactive element in the DevTools Accessibility pane or with a screen reader. Confirm it exposes a meaningful name, the correct role, and current states and values such as expanded, checked or selected, and that changes are announced.

name: Status Messages
howToTest: Trigger status updates such as form success messages, search result counts, cart updates and loading indicators. Confirm a screen reader announces them without focus moving, for example through role="status" or aria-live.
